corpus.title: What Did US Envoys Achieve in Moscow and Kyiv?
corpus.signal_text:
US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow and with Ukrainian President Volodomyr Zelensky in Kyiv on the weekend to discuss how to end the war between the two countries. Afterwards, Witkoff called on both sides to make compromises. Zelensky said that security and economic guarantees for Ukraine had been discussed. Moscow described the talks as “extremely frank” and “constructive”.

Time is on Putin’s side
Journalist and former deputy minister for infrastructure Mustafa Nayyem (Ukraine) analyses the situation on Facebook:
“Donald Trump has made his ability to bring wars to a swift end an integral part of his political image. Furthermore, the political calendar is piling on the pressure: the mid-term elections are just around the corner and the presidential election campaign begins about a year from now. ... The more urgently Washington needs results, the more sense it makes for Moscow to play for time, continue the war and wait for the next offer. This is why I would focus less on the number of visits by Witkoff and instead ask what has changed in Putin’s calculations after each of these visits. Right now the answer seems to be pretty clear: nothing.”

corpus.title: Russia says it hopes US-mediated talks with Ukraine will resume soon
corpus.signal_text:
Russia says it hopes US-mediated talks with Ukraine will resume soon
MOSCOW, Sept 9 - Russia hopes that U.S.-mediated peace talks on ending the war in Ukraine will resume soon, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Wednesday.
No such talks between Russia and Ukraine have taken place since February, but President Donald Trump sent his negotiators to Moscow and then Kyiv at the weekend in a bid to relaunch the stalled process.
Peskov was responding to a comment by U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio that it may be possible to draw up a roadmap to restart talks and work towards an acceptable outcome for both sides.
A huge gulf remains between Russia and Ukraine on how to end the 4-1/2-year war, with Kyiv rejecting Moscow's demands that it give up more territory.
Peskov said Moscow would not publicly discuss any specifics of a potential settlement, but there was a "confirmed political will" to resume talks.
"We hope that these negotiations will resume in the foreseeable future, and we remain in contact with our American counterparts," he said, a day after Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin spoke by phone.
Peskov added that the issue of exchanging prisoners between Russia and the U.S. was "a constant item on the agenda", including between the two presidents. He noted that Russia had released one American prisoner, Robert Gilman, at Trump's request last month.
The two countries have traded prisoners at several points in the past few years.
The biggest such deal was in August 2024, when Russia got back eight prisoners held in the West, including a member of its FSB security service convicted of murder in Germany.
In exchange, 16 people were released from Russian and Belarusian jails. Among those freed by Moscow were prominent Russian dissidents and three U.S. citizens, including Wall Street Journal correspondent Evan Gershkovich. REUTERS

corpus.signal_text:
Kremlin says there is currently no formal plan to end war against Ukraine
There is currently no formal plan or roadmap for settling Russia's war against Ukraine, but Moscow hopes to resume trilateral talks, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov has said.
Source: Kremlin-aligned Russian news agency Interfax
Quote from Peskov: "We would not want to, and will not, discuss any points in public, especially since there are currently no, so to speak, formalised, coherent programmes or roadmaps."
Details: Meanwhile, he added that there is a "general initiative and political desire" to resume trilateral talks, and that this has been confirmed.
"We hope that these talks will resume in the near future," the spokesman said.
Background:
- US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said earlier that a roadmap for resuming negotiations between Russia and Ukraine could be drawn up in the coming weeks.
- President Volodymyr Zelenskyy believes there is a possibility that another round of trilateral talks between the US, Ukraine and Russia may be held, although no decision has been made yet.
- Zelenskyy said after meeting the US envoys that he had received a message from them: "the Russians are ready to negotiate".
